newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House Republican leader backs SPR oil sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House Republican leader backs SPR oil sale.

text.p: U.S. House Majority Leader Richard Armey said Tuesday he backed a plan in a House spending bill to sell $209 million of oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.

A $13 billion spending bill for a number of federal land and energy programs that the full House is to consider later this week would sell $209 million worth of oil from the reserve to help cover its operating costs.
Asked if he would object to the sale, Armey, a Texas Republican, told reporters, "I don't have a problem with that."
Congress has authorized sales of about 30 million barrels from the reserve in recent years to help defray the budget deficit and cover the reserve's operating costs.
Energy Secretary Federico Pena has said he opposed further sales from the reserve, which he said must be maintained at a sufficient level to help stabilize oil markets in case of a supply disruption.
The reserve was established in the 1970s in the wake of the Middle East oil embargo that roiled markets.
